patient.name: Hannah Lee
patient.affectEn: frightened and drowsy; slumped sideways in a restaurant booth, flushed, face and lips obviously swollen, one hand clutching her throat; audible wheeze and stridor
patient.speechEn: can only manage one or two words at a time between breaths ('can't... breathe'); her friend answers most history questions for her. After epinephrine she improves and can talk in short sentences.

scene.settingEn: A busy Thai restaurant in New Westminster at 1915 hrs. Staff have cleared a path to a corner booth. Room temperature, no hazards. One patient. Her friend sits beside her still holding the plate of pad thai she was eating.
hazardsEn: ongoing allergen exposure: the plate of pad thai (the suspected peanut source) is still right in front of her

bystanders.knowsEn: She took her first mouthful of the pad thai about 8 minutes ago; she told the server 'no peanuts'. Within 2 minutes she said she was itchy and her throat felt tight, then her face and lips started swelling. She has a known peanut anaphylaxis: two previous ER visits and she has used an EpiPen once before. She also has mild asthma and uses a salbutamol inhaler when she needs it. Her EpiPen is not with her tonight and it expired last month. Allergies: peanuts (anaphylaxis) and shellfish (hives). She has had only the pad thai and water. Does not know anything else.
They called 911 and cleared a path to the booth. They know nothing about her medical history. They will hold doors or move tables if asked.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
bag-valve mask with oral and nasal airways
epinephrine for IM injection, with syringes and IM needles
PCP only: IV start kit with normal saline

dispatchEn: 1915 hrs. Code 3 to a Thai restaurant in New Westminster. 24-year-old female with a known peanut allergy has an allergic reaction. Staff say she is having trouble breathing. Hospital is 9 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: caller says her face is swelling and she used to carry an EpiPen but does not have it tonight.
arrivalEn: Restaurant staff meet you at the door; they have cleared a path through the busy dining room to a corner booth. Room temperature, no hazards. One patient: a young woman slumped sideways in the booth. Her friend is beside her, still holding a plate of pad thai.
firstLookEn: A 24-year-old woman slumped sideways in the booth, flushed, with obvious facial and lip swelling. You can hear wheeze and stridor from where you stand. She clutches her throat, too short of breath to say more than a word or two.

primary.locEn: Drowsy and confused; responds to your voice (AVPU = V). Eyes open, answers in one or two words only, clutching her throat: "Can't... breathe."
primary.airwayEn: Lips and tongue swollen, stridor present, but she is still moving air. No vomit, no blood, no foreign body in the mouth.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 30, laboured, with accessory muscle use and audible wheeze. Chest rises equally.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 130, weak, regular. No external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey for a medical patient: no trauma, no injection sites, no stinger. Widespread urticaria (hives) over the chest and arms. Skin flushed, warm and moist (skin is given automatically during the RBS). C-spine not indicated - no trauma.
primary.skinEn: flushed, widespread urticaria (hives) over chest and arms, warm and moist

history.ccEn: Throat... closing. Can't... breathe. (Friend: "She's having an allergic reaction - her throat is swelling and she can't breathe.")

opqrst.oEn: Peanuts... the noodles. (Friend: "Her first mouthful of the pad thai was about 8 minutes ago. She told the server no peanuts. Within 2 minutes she was itchy and said her throat felt tight, then her face started swelling.")
opqrst.pEn: Nothing... helps. (Friend: "Nothing has made it better.")
opqrst.qEn: Tight... throat. Itchy. (Friend: "She says her throat feels tight and she's itchy.")
opqrst.rEn: Throat... face. (Friend: "Her face and lips are swelling, and she's got hives on her chest and arms.")
opqrst.sEn: Worst... ever. (Friend: "She says this is the worst reaction she's ever had - worse than the two times she went to the ER.")
opqrst.tEn: Sudden. Getting... worse. (Friend: "It came on all at once, within 2 minutes of eating, and the swelling has kept getting worse.")

history.painScoreEn: She shakes her head: "Not... pain. Can't... breathe." (No numeric pain score is given in this scenario.)

sample.sEn: Throat tight... can't breathe... itchy. (Friend: "Her face and lips are swelling and she's covered in hives.")
sample.aEn: Peanuts. (Friend: "Peanuts - that's anaphylaxis for her. And shellfish gives her hives.")
sample.mEn: Puffer. (Friend: "A salbutamol inhaler when she needs it. She has an EpiPen but it's not with her tonight - it expired last month.")
sample.pEn: Peanuts... asthma. (Friend: "Peanut anaphylaxis - she's been to the ER twice for it and used her EpiPen once before. And mild asthma.")
sample.lEn: Noodles... water. (Friend: "Just the pad thai, right now, and water.")
sample.eEn: Ate... pad thai. (Friend: "We were having dinner. She told the server no peanuts. About 2 minutes after her first mouthful she got itchy and her throat went tight.")

fe.respiratoryEn: My throat was tight and I was wheezing. It's getting better now.
fe.giGuEn: My stomach is crampy and I feel sick to my stomach.
fe.integumentaryEn: I'm itchy all over and I've got hives everywhere.
fe.endocrineEn: No, nothing like that. No diabetes, no thyroid problems.
fe.eentEn: My lips and tongue are swollen, and my eyes are itchy and puffy.

findings.headNeckEn: Lip and tongue swelling (angioedema); eyes puffy. Stridor present before epinephrine; once epinephrine has been given the stridor is decreasing. No JVD.
findings.chestLungsEn: Expiratory wheeze in all fields on 6-site auscultation, equal both sides; the wheeze improves after salbutamol (only if salbutamol has been given). Urticaria across the chest.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft, with mild generalized tenderness. No distension.
findings.backEn: Urticaria across the back. No other findings.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: Urticaria on both legs. Circulation, sensation and movement intact.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Urticaria on both arms. Circulation, sensation and movement intact.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: baseline, before epinephrine (required before initiating the protocol); unchanged until epinephrine has had time to work
about 5 minutes after epinephrine, en route; improving (stridor resolved, wheeze reduced) - document the response

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: She is not improving: still drowsy and confused, stridor and wheeze persist, still flushed with hives, pulse still weak.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan epinephrine, oxygen, salbutamol, BVM, early transport
triggers: bring the epi and the airway kit

expected.actionEn: Recognize from dispatch this is likely an unstable anaphylaxis call
triggers: she's going to be a priority patient

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (none), environment, nature of illness (allergic reaction / possible ongoing allergen), number of patients (1)
triggers: nature of illness is an allergic reaction
is she still eating the food

triggers: putting on gloves and eye protection

expected.actionEn: Remove/stop the allergen exposure (clear the food away)

expected.actionEn: Assess LOC / AVPU: responds to Verbal, drowsy - a decreased LOC finding
Verbalize c-spine not indicated (medical, no trauma)
Assess airway - identify swelling and stridor as an airway threat
Assess breathing - rate, effort, accessory muscle use, wheeze

Note skin: flushed, urticaria, warm moist
High-flow oxygen 15 L NRB to target SpO2 at or above 94%
Position SUPINE to support blood pressure and do NOT walk the patient (per Anaphylaxis guideline)

expected.actionEn: Categorize as RTC and act with urgency
Epinephrine given on scene, then ready to load within 15 minutes
triggers: give the epi here then transport

expected.actionEn: Delegate crew members to prep egress (explicitly required by the Anaphylaxis guideline)
triggers: bring the stretcher to the booth
clear a path to the door

expected.actionEn: Establish chief complaint: difficulty breathing and throat swelling after eating
triggers: can you tell me what's wrong

expected.actionEn: HxC/C with OPQRRRST/LOTARP: onset, allergen, time from exposure, progression, previous reactions, severity
PMHx (peanut anaphylaxis, asthma)

Allergies with consequence detail

Use the friend as a history source when the patient cannot speak

Pulse rate/strength/rhythm

SpO2 with calibration

FE - Respiratory (pertinent)
FE - Cardiovascular

FE - Musculoskeletal

Abdomen exam
Back exam

Initiate the Anaphylaxis protocol with correct indications (signs + exposure + instability) and baseline vitals done
triggers: she meets the criteria for epi
baseline vitals are done so I'll give epi

expected.actionEn: Administer epinephrine 0.5 mg IM with the 6 rights, correct site (anterolateral thigh) and IM needle
triggers: right patient right drug right dose

expected.actionEn: Verbalize repeat dosing: may repeat 0.5 mg IM every 5 minutes up to 3 doses if no improvement
triggers: if no improvement I'll repeat the epi

expected.actionEn: PCP: salbutamol for bronchospasm only AFTER epinephrine; diphenhydramine 25-50 mg; IV with fluid bolus if still hypotensive
Do not allow the patient to stand or walk to the stretcher
triggers: we'll lift you onto the stretcher

expected.actionEn: Reassess ABCs and all interventions after epinephrine and after each move
Second full set of vitals within 5-6 minutes and interpret the response to epinephrine
Verbalize the plan for a repeat dose if deterioration or no improvement occurs
triggers: if she gets worse I'll give another epi

expected.actionEn: En-route notification for a critical patient
Complete hand-off with epinephrine time, dose, route and response
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate lets the patient stand up or walk (e.g. walks her to the stretcher, the door or the ambulance)
candidate deliberately positions the patient sitting upright (sits her up, high or semi-Fowler's on the cot) while she is still hypotensive, instead of supine
candidate gives epinephrine at a dose other than 0.5 mg (adult)
candidate gives epinephrine by a route other than IM (e.g. IV, subcutaneous)
PCP runs the saline bolus past 500 mL or onto the next bag without reassessing the patient (BP / vitals / ABCs) in between

drugs.doseEn: 0.5 mg IM (adult), anterolateral thigh, after baseline vitals; may repeat every 5 minutes up to 3 times if no improvement
drugs.indicationsEn: anaphylaxis: signs of anaphylaxis + exposure to an allergen + unstable (decreased LOC, BP < 90 mmHg, respiratory distress) - all present here
drugs.contraindicationsEn: no absolute contraindications in life-threatening situations such as anaphylaxis
drugs.cautionsEn: further hypotension if administered too quickly

drugs.doseEn: 5 mg by nebulizer, or MDI 4 x 100 mcg (adult); repeat as required - for bronchospasm ONLY AFTER epinephrine has been given
25-50 mg IM, IV or PO - adjunct to limit the histamine response, ONLY AFTER epinephrine
20 mL/kg IV bolus to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL, if she remains hypotensive or hypoperfused

notificationFacts.vitals: baseline GCS 14, BP 84/50, pulse 130 weak, resp 30 laboured with wheeze, SpO2 88% on room air; 5 minutes after epinephrine GCS 15, BP 106/68, pulse 118, resp 22, SpO2 96% on 15 L NRB

notificationFacts.findings: stridor (resolved after epinephrine), wheeze, facial and lip angioedema, widespread urticaria, abdominal cramping and nausea

examinerPrompts.locNotDepictedEn: She is drowsy and confused: she opens her eyes and responds to your voice, but only manages one or two words.
examinerPrompts.breathingNotDepictedEn: She is working hard to breathe: laboured, with accessory muscle use, audible wheeze and stridor.

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR gives epinephrine 0.5 mg IM (repeat q5 min up to 3 doses), oxygen, supine positioning, delegates egress prep and transports rapidly. EMR does NOT give diphenhydramine or IV fluids. Salbutamol for bronchospasm is acceptable at EMR level (SOB with Asthma/COPD protocol; she is a known asthmatic) but only AFTER epinephrine. No Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds vascular access with a 20 mL/kg bolus (max 2 L, reassess q500 mL) if she remains hypotensive or hypoperfused, salbutamol after epinephrine for bronchospasm, diphenhydramine 25-50 mg, and the 9-system Functional Enquiry en route.

sourcePages: Scenario md-01 (data/practical/scenarios.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing, handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (altered LOC, respiratory distress, anaphylaxis = unstable); p.49 SOB with History of Asthma/COPD (salbutamol at all licence levels); p.50 Oxygen Administration (SOB or shock = high-flow O2, NRB 15 L/min); p.55 Anaphylaxis (indications: signs + allergen exposure + unstable incl. BP < 90 mmHg; supine and do not walk; remove allergen; SpO2 >= 94%; delegate egress; history and baseline vitals; epinephrine; PCP: vascular access with 20 mL/kg bolus to a maximum of 2 L reassessing every 500 mL, salbutamol after epinephrine, diphenhydramine); p.64 Diphenhydramine (25-50 mg IM/IV/PO); p.66 Epinephrine (adult 0.5 mg IM every 5 minutes, may repeat up to 3 times; no absolute contraindications in anaphylaxis; caution further hypotension); p.77 Salbutamol (5 mg nebulized, MDI 4 x 100 mcg adult; anaphylaxis bronchospasm).
